packages.name: FFmpeg
packages.summary: Current upstream ffmpeg CLI compiled as a generic, full-featured browser WebAssembly distribution.

upstream.license: LGPL-2.1-or-later / GPL-2.0-or-later depending on enabled components

profiles.label: Browser Full
profiles.output: Generic ffmpeg CLI; output is chosen by CLI arguments
profiles.size: Loaded from the published release manifest

profiles.label: Browser Full GPL
profiles.output: Generic ffmpeg CLI with GPL/libx264 features
profiles.size: Loaded from the published release manifest

integration.summary: Download one FFmpeg profile ZIP, extract it under your app, and point the thin runtime wrapper at the matching core files.
integration.example:
<script src="/vendor/ffmpeg/browser-ffmpeg.js"></script>
<script type="module">
async function remuxMp4(file) {
  const ffmpeg = await WasmZooFFmpeg.loadHosted({
    coreJsUrl: "/vendor/ffmpeg/ffmpeg-core.js",
    wasmUrl: "/vendor/ffmpeg/ffmpeg-core.wasm"
  });

  try {
    const result = await ffmpeg.exec(
      ["-i", "/input.mp4", "-c", "copy", "/output.mp4"],
      {
        files: [{ name: "/input.mp4", data: file }],
        outputs: ["/output.mp4"],
        onLog: ({ stream, message }) => console.log(stream, message)
      }
    );
    return result.files[0].data;
  } finally {
    ffmpeg.dispose();
  }
}
</script>
notes: Both full profiles require SharedArrayBuffer and cross-origin isolation (COOP/COEP).
browser-full and browser-full-gpl use the same wrapper API and filenames; choose the GPL build only when you need its extra GPL components such as libx264.
Input and output paths are Emscripten MEMFS paths for each command.

packages.name: ImageMagick
packages.summary: Upstream magick CLI compiled for browser WebAssembly with reproducible source and toolchain pins.

profiles.label: Browser Full
profiles.output: Generic upstream magick CLI; input and output paths are chosen by CLI arguments
profiles.size: Loaded from the published release manifest

integration.summary: Self-host the ImageMagick release files and use the wrapper to run ordinary magick CLI arguments against in-memory files.
integration.example:
<script src="/vendor/imagemagick/browser-imagemagick.js"></script>
<script type="module">
async function resizeToJpeg(file) {
  const magick = WasmZooImageMagick.loadHosted({
    baseUrl: "/vendor/imagemagick/"
  });

  try {
    const result = await magick.exec(
      ["/input.png", "-resize", "640x640>", "/out/output.jpg"],
      {
        files: [{ name: "/input.png", data: file }],
        dirs: ["/out"],
        outputs: ["/out/output.jpg"]
      }
    );
    return result.files[0].data;
  } finally {
    magick.dispose();
  }
}
</script>
notes: No SharedArrayBuffer or cross-origin isolation is required for browser-full.
v0.4.0 intentionally focuses on PNG/JPEG conversion, identify and basic image transforms; unsupported delegates remain documented in the package notes.
Input and output paths are MEMFS paths and the returned file data is a Uint8Array.

comparison.name: Upstream native
comparison.note: Feature set depends on optional delegate libraries and platform integration available in the native build.

comparison.name: WASM Zoo
comparison.note: Upstream magick CLI with browser filesystem constraints and PNG/JPEG-focused delegate set.

notes: The browser-full profile is deliberately single-threaded: ImageMagick thread support and OpenMP are disabled, the CLI runs inside an outer Worker, and SharedArrayBuffer/cross-origin isolation are not required.
Files live in Emscripten MEMFS during each command; native filesystem watches, device access, fonts and shell pipes are not equivalent to a desktop build.
ImageMagick zero-configuration mode is enabled so the browser build does not depend on external delegates.xml/config files.
v0.4.0 enables zlib, PNG and JPEG support. Optional delegates such as TIFF, WebP, HEIC, OpenEXR, LCMS, XML, Ghostscript/PDF and font stacks remain disabled and are recorded as capability gaps.
The real Chromium smoke test runs magick -version, identifies a PNG fixture, resizes it and writes a JPEG output.
Pages stages the published release core and uses the current runtime wrapper for the Playground, matching the FFmpeg/libarchive pattern.

ImageMagick 7.1.2 detects PNG through pkg-config; Emscripten 6.0.6 provides libpng 1.6.58 without libpng.pc, so the builder supplies a target-only pkg-config shim that points back to the pinned Emscripten port.

The browser-full builder applies a narrowly scoped source patch for zero-configuration mode: the one-time anonymous pixel-cache mmap decision is initialized to disabled. With an empty built-in policy and no working Emscripten mmap this preserves the effective behavior while avoiding ImageMagick's policy/semaphore initialization cycle during first pixel-cache open.

packages.name: libarchive
packages.summary: Upstream archive command-line tools compiled for browser WebAssembly with reproducible source and toolchain pins.

profiles.label: Browser Full
profiles.output: Four generic upstream archive CLIs; archive files are chosen by CLI arguments
profiles.size: Loaded from the published release manifest

integration.summary: Self-host the runtime wrapper plus the core pair for each libarchive CLI you use. This example extracts a ZIP with bsdtar.
integration.example:
<script src="/vendor/libarchive/browser-libarchive.js"></script>
<script type="module">
async function extractZip(file) {
  const archive = WasmZooLibarchive.loadHosted({
    baseUrl: "/vendor/libarchive/"
  });

  try {
    const result = await archive.exec(
      "bsdtar",
      ["-xf", "/input.zip", "-C", "/out"],
      {
        files: [{ name: "/input.zip", data: file }],
        dirs: ["/out"],
        collectDirs: ["/out"]
      }
    );
    return result.files;
  } finally {
    archive.dispose();
  }
}
</script>
notes: No SharedArrayBuffer or cross-origin isolation is required for the browser-full profile.
For bsdcpio, bsdcat or bsdunzip, also host the matching <tool>-core.js and <tool>-core.wasm pair.
Extracted files are returned from MEMFS as Uint8Array data.

packages.name: libvips
packages.summary: Upstream libvips image-processing library compiled for browser WebAssembly with a pinned Emscripten adapter.

profiles.label: Browser Core
features: resize / thumbnail / colourspace / composite / convolution operations
TIFF / GIF / imagequant / quantizr / legacy PPM-Analyze-Radiance loaders removed
externalLibraries: GLib, mozjpeg, libpng, libwebp and required dependencies built by the pinned wasm-vips recipe
profiles.output: Smaller generic libvips JavaScript API for JPEG/PNG/WebP Browser-Kitty-style image workflows
profiles.size: Loaded from the published release manifest

profiles.label: Browser Full
features: JPEG / PNG / WebP / TIFF / GIF raster processing
resize / thumbnail / colourspace / composite / convolution operations
externalLibraries: GLib and image codec dependencies built by the pinned wasm-vips recipe
profiles.output: Generic libvips JavaScript API with JPEG/PNG/WebP plus TIFF/GIF support
profiles.size: Loaded from the published release manifest

integration.summary: Use browser-core for JPEG/PNG/WebP by default; choose browser-full only when TIFF/GIF support is needed. Both expose the same upstream-style libvips API.
integration.example:
<script src="/vendor/libvips/browser-core/browser-libvips.js"></script>
<script type="module">
async function resizeToJpeg(file, width = 640) {
  const vips = await WasmZooLibvips.loadHosted({
    baseUrl: "/vendor/libvips/browser-core/"
  });

  const input = vips.Image.newFromBuffer(new Uint8Array(await file.arrayBuffer()));
  const resized = input.resize(width / input.width);
  const output = resized.writeToBuffer(".jpg[Q=85]");
  resized.delete();
  input.delete();
  return output;
}
</script>
notes: browser-core is the recommended Browser-Kitty profile: JPEG/PNG/WebP only, with TIFF/GIF/imagequant/quantizr and legacy PPM/Analyze/Radiance loaders removed.
browser-full adds TIFF/GIF/imagequant while keeping the same JavaScript API.
Both profiles require SharedArrayBuffer and cross-origin isolation (COOP/COEP) because libvips uses pthreads.
The raw vips.js API is the primary distribution. browser-libvips.js is only a self-hosting convenience loader.
The browser adapter and both Emscripten/libvips compatibility patch heads are pinned to immutable commits.
AVIF/HEIC, JPEG XL, SVG/resvg and UltraHDR are intentionally disabled in v0.5.0.

comparison.name: Upstream native

packages.name: Ghostscript
packages.summary: Current upstream Ghostscript PostScript/PDF CLI compiled for browser WebAssembly with an isolated-worker MEMFS runtime.

profiles.label: Browser Full
features: BMP / JPEG / PNG / PS / TIFF output-driver groups
externalLibraries: Ghostscript bundled third-party source set from the official 10.07.1 release archive
profiles.output: Generic Ghostscript gs CLI for local PostScript/PDF rendering and conversion
profiles.size: Loaded from the published release manifest

integration.summary: Self-host the wrapper plus gs-core.js/gs-core.wasm and run ordinary Ghostscript CLI arguments against files in MEMFS.
integration.example:
<script src="/vendor/ghostscript/browser-ghostscript.js"></script>
<script type="module">
const gs = WasmZooGhostscript.loadHosted({ baseUrl: "/vendor/ghostscript/" });
try {
  const result = await gs.exec([
    "-dSAFER", "-dBATCH", "-dNOPAUSE",
    "-sDEVICE=png16m", "-r150",
    "-sOutputFile=/out/page.png", "/input.pdf"
  ], {
    files: [{ name: "/input.pdf", data: file }],
    dirs: ["/out"],
    outputs: ["/out/page.png"]
  });
  return result.files[0].data;
} finally {
  gs.dispose();
}
</script>
notes: The current browser-full profile is single-threaded and does not require SharedArrayBuffer.
Each command runs in a fresh Worker/MEMFS instance.
The published Ghostscript Wasm binary is AGPL-3.0-or-later; review licensing before redistribution.

comparison.name: Upstream native
comparison.note: Full native Ghostscript can integrate with operating-system print/display services and optional platform libraries.

comparison.name: WASM Zoo
comparison.note: Current Ghostscript gs CLI with browser-oriented file-output devices and native desktop integrations removed.

notes: Official Ghostscript 10.07.1 release source archive is pinned by SHA-256 in addition to the source branch commit.
The real Chromium smoke test renders a PDF to PNG and converts PostScript to PDF with pdfwrite.
Automatic upstream candidate substitution is intentionally disabled for Ghostscript until the watcher also captures and verifies the new official source-asset digest.
GhostPCL and GhostXPS remain outside this package even though they share the GhostPDL source tree.
